advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `parts.port` access in `instance_from_base_url` so an invalid port yields `""` (or omits the port) rather than letting `ValueError` propagate.
evidence: Docstring promise at deployment.py:44-45: 'a backend that cannot name its deployment should degrade to "unnamed" rather than make the backend unbuildable'
`urllib.parse.SplitResult.port` raises ValueError on a non-numeric or out-of-range port substring (stdlib, resolved: /usr/local/lib/python3.12/urllib/parse.py)

The factories call this at construction time: `instance=instance_from_base_url(settings.url)` (jira_datacenter/backend.py:196) and `instance=instance_from_base_url(s.url)` (jira/backend.py:293), so a malformed configured port crashes build_backend

ABSENCE: `test_an_unusable_base_url_degrades_to_empty_rather_than_raising` only tests `""`, `"   "`, `"://"` (test_remote_ref_deployment_heldout.py:61) — none reach the `.port` access, so the raising path is untested
advisory.finding: `instance_from_base_url` accesses `parts.port`, which raises `ValueError` for a present-but-invalid port (non-numeric like `host:abc`, or out-of-range like `host:99999`). That exception propagates out of the helper, breaking its documented 'returns "" rather than raising' contract and turning a cosmetic label derivation into a `build_backend` construction crash.
scenarios: An operator configures a base URL with a typo'd/invalid port (e.g. `https://jira.example.com:0/jira` or `https://jira.example.com:abc`) and backend construction raises ValueError instead of degrading to an unnamed instance
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the `parts.port` access in a try/except ValueError, returning "" (or treating port as None) on failure; add a parametrized test case covering an invalid/out-of-range port.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that builds a backend through the build_backend factory (mocking settings resolution) and asserts remote_ref() returns the normalized instance derived from the configured URL, covering the factory→constructor wiring.
evidence: New test `_real_backends()` constructs backends directly: `JiraBackend(transport=_StubTransport(), instance=instance)` (test file lines 87-90) — the factory path is never invoked.

Existing factory tests (test_transport_port_completeness_heldout.py:293-347) assert only conformance failures via `pytest.raises(backend_mod.BackendEnvError)`, which fires at `assert_transport_conforms` (backend.py:194) BEFORE the `instance=instance_from_base_url(...)` line at 195-196 is reached.

ABSENCE: no test asserts that a factory-built backend's remote_ref() carries the instance derived from the configured URL; a regression dropping/misrouting the instance= argument in either factory would pass the whole suite.
advisory.finding: The build_backend factory wiring that passes the normalized instance (instance_from_base_url(url)) into the backend constructor is untested. All backend tests construct backends directly with an explicit instance, and the existing factory tests raise a conformance error before the instance is derived, so a factory that dropped the instance= kwarg or passed the raw un-normalized URL would not be caught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a factory-level test for each vendor that monkeypatches settings resolution to return a concrete url (e.g. 'https://jira.example.com/jira'), calls the build_backend factory, and asserts backend.remote_ref('DIG-1').instance == instance_from_base_url(that_url) — proving the factory both invokes the normalizer and threads the result into the constructor.
